[engine] A comment that explains WHY a mechanism exists reads exactly like a description of the current state, so it cannot be used to conclude 'X is still the case'. Before drawing a status conclusion from a comment, resolve the FLAG the comment names and read that flag's own state -- and look for a loud warning emitted alongside it. A comment about a decoupling describes what it decouples FROM, which is the past, not the present.

**class**: `source-reading`

## 為什麼（because）

Fell for it on the CGC_POOL_SPLIT comment in llama-model-loader.h: it says the split keeps the expert tensors at full width and then explains '... which is exactly the coupling that forces n_batch down to cgc_pool_max_tokens() when the tensor is shrunk'. Reading that second half as the present tense produced a wrong status report -- 'M1 has not started' about a work item that was in fact implemented and separately judged unusable. The truth was in a different file, two lines of a WARN: llama.cpp emits 'CGC_POOL_SPLIT is an EXPERIMENTAL, NOT USABLE configuration' with its measured failure (M1 2/42, 234 buffer-is-nil, warmup OOM at both 10 GiB and 4 GiB on a 16 GB box). The same nominal status also exists in the roadmap's own record, which says the numeric gate was ACHIEVED -- the two sources only look contradictory until you notice they describe different work items.

## 反例（counterexample_observed）

Corrected within the hour against docs/roadmap-2026-09-14/ROADMAP_PREFILL250_DECODE25_2026-09-14.html, which records M1's numeric gate as reached (M1=M2=M3=117/117 at 2/4/6/8/10 GiB, including the union>slots case at 2 GiB) while listing two exit conditions still open (decode must not regress -- measured 0.72x; prefill chunk 2048 -- needs work item 2, which does not exist). Related trap, same repo: 'M1/M2/M3' names both roadmap milestones and the D5 gate's three verdict metrics, so a status question about one reads as a status question about the other.

## 適用於（applies_to）

- `src/llama.cpp/src/llama-model-loader.h`
- `src/llama.cpp/src/llama.cpp`
